title: Fixed Pierced Slat Chain and Loop Handles Binzasara
description: One newly authored complete binzasara-inspired strung-slat percussion appearance held in a low U-shaped static pose. Nineteen complete flat wooden-look blades each have an actual small through-bore near one short end, full broad faces and finite cut-edge thickness. One entire capped longitudinal curved cord passes through every bore; each blade has a small explicit lower-bore static seating contact and a visible unfilled upper bore crescent. At both ends the cord meets a whole closed oval leather-look loop grip with real open interior. The slats fan away from the linked end route and leave real air gaps; there is no supporting frame or backing sheet. Every pierced plate, station transform, longitudinal route and grip loop is independently authored numeric geometry. This is not the older makisu bent into a different arc: that complete mat has unperforated transverse bamboo rods held by four external returning over-under lacing circuits. It is not a Jacob-ladder block-count variant: that toy has thick unperforated tiles with three broad ribbons alternating across opposite faces. Here all near-end bores belong to the full blades and one connecting cord traverses those holes, rather than wrapping around the faces; complete end grip loops are integral to the new organization. Twenty-two closed editable whole meshes, four opaque constant untextured PBR roles, metres native Z up and whole horizontal-bounds-centred ground datum. One whole independent model zero scenes; no separate blade or handle count. Broad category inspiration only, not a measured museum replica or historically authenticated object. The U pose and finite bottom face are a neutral static display arrangement, not an unsupported equilibrium claim. Cord contact, hole clearance and attachment overlaps are simplified fixed visual joints, not a tested flexible tether. No sound, wave motion, striking sequence, traditional performance, grip comfort, cord tension, material authenticity, articulation, balance, load, fabrication or safety claim; no hands, rig, animation or interaction.
